summary: IBM originated from Herman Hollerith's punch card tabulating machines used in the 1890 US Census. Four companies merged into Computing-Tabulating-Recording Company (CTR) in 1911, renamed International Business Machines in 1924 under Thomas J. Watson Sr.

System/360 announced April 7 1964 was the first family of compatible computers where software written for one model ran on all. Cost $5B to develop. Fixed the 8-bit byte as standard. Became the dominant mainframe and industry standard within two years.

In 1969 IBM unbundled software and services from hardware, charging separately for programs and education. This single decision created the independent software industry. Before this software was free with the machine.

IBM PC announced August 12 1981 from Boca Raton Florida. Used off-the-shelf Intel 8088 and Microsoft DOS. Open architecture spawned clone industry. IBM did not own the processor or OS, which transferred monopolistic power to Microsoft and Intel.

Deep Blue defeated world chess champion Garry Kasparov in 1997, first computer to beat a reigning world champion under tournament rules. Evaluated 200 million positions per second. Demonstrated computing could solve complex strategic problems.

IBM Watson won Jeopardy! in 2011 against champions Ken Jennings and Brad Rutter. Named after IBM's first CEO Thomas J. Watson. 2880 processor cores, understood natural language questions and answered in under 3 seconds.

watsonx is IBM's AI and data platform launched May 2023. Granite models are open-sourced under Apache 2.0, 3-34B parameters, designed for code generation, time-series forecasting, and document processing. IBM has 70+ years of AI research from checkers to chess to Jeopardy to enterprise.

IBM inventor Robert Dennard created DRAM in 1966-68: one transistor and one capacitor per bit. Replaced designs needing six transistors. This is why memory is bought by gigabytes today. Dennard also authored the scaling rule that governed chip design for 30 years.

Edgar Codd at IBM San Jose published the relational database model in 1970. IBM built System R to test it, producing SQL. Oracle reached market first. SQL is now the standard query language for nearly every business system worldwide.

FORTRAN delivered in 1957 by John Backus at IBM. First high-level programming language for scientific computing. Argued programmers should not write in machine instruction sets. Still used in scientific computing 70 years later.

John Cocke at IBM Yorktown developed RISC (Reduced Instruction Set Computing) starting 1974. Argument: fewer instructions executed fast beats many instructions executed slow. POWER architecture in RS/6000 is descendant. Same reasoning shaped phone processors for 30 years.

IBM researchers have won 5 Nobel Prizes in physics, 4 Turing Awards, 5 National Medals of Technology, 5 National Medals of Science. Zurich lab alone produced 2 Nobels in consecutive years (1986 STM, 1987 superconductivity).

IBM acquired Red Hat for $34B in 2018-2019, its largest acquisition ever. Refocused IBM on hybrid cloud computing and AI. Red Hat operates within IBM's Hybrid Cloud division. Enabled IBM to shift from hardware to services and cloud.

IBM put a 5-qubit quantum processor on the public internet in 2016, years before a market existed. Funds quantum research from enterprise business. Pattern: IBM repeatedly destroys its own best business before competitors do, from punch cards to mainframes to PC to quantum.

IBM faced 20+ antitrust actions in the 20th century. 1956 consent decree forced selling equipment (not just leasing), licensing patents, enabling competitors. 1969 US v IBM ran 13 years, dropped 1982 as without merit. Unbundling in 1969 was partly in response to antitrust pressure.

IBM built SAGE air defense computers for US Air Force in 1950s. Each AN/FSQ-7 weighed 250 tons. SAGE accounted for 80% of IBM computing revenue 1952-1955. Taught IBM real-time computing, magnetic core memory, and data transmission years before commercial market existed.

IBM's German subsidiary Dehomag supplied Hollerith equipment to Nazi regime for censuses and population registration. Contested whether IBM NY maintained oversight. Edwin Black's 2001 book argued IBM profited and directed. IBM says subsidiary was seized by Nazis. No court has ruled on substance. Historians divided.

Louis Gerstner became IBM CEO in 1993, first outsider since 1914. IBM lost $16B 1991-1993. Gerstner reversed plan to split IBM into separate companies, kept it whole for integrated solutions advantage. Shed commodity businesses, built services and software. Profitable by 1994.
